Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1030 AM EDT Mon Aug 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
With the expectation of decreasing coverage of heavy rainfall,
have shifted wording to mention south of I-66. Any flash
flooding threat likely focuses closer to the I-64 corridor.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Additional heavy rainfall is possible this afternoon and
  evening, mainly south of I-66.

- 2) Additional shower and thunderstorm chances persist through
  this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE...Additional heavy rainfall is possible this
afternoon and evening, mainly south of I-66.

The earlier upper low across the Ohio Valley has now shifted
just north of Lake Ontario while becoming more elongated in
nature. At the same time, this has pushed the parent frontal
boundary along I-81 where it has generally stalled. The forecast
calls for this frontal system to slowly drop southward in time.
The front is going to be the main focus for another round of 
showers and thunderstorms. The main uncertainty is the exact 
placement of this boundary, with most high res guidance showing 
it south of I-66 where low-level convergence is more focused. 
This is where most of the rain chances (50-70 pct) will be for 
today, with mostly dry conditions to the north/west.

It is still going to be warm and muggy areawide as highs reach the 
mid to upper 80s. Thunderstorms once again are going to be efficient 
rain makers with a deep warm cloud layer and PWATs above 2". A few 
instances of flash flooding are possible if any heavy thunderstorm 
develops and moves slowly over regions of poor drainage. The 
frontal boundary completely crosses the area this evening, 
ushering in drier conditions for tonight. Slightly lower dew 
points allow temps to drop to the 60s for most locations (upper 
50s in the mountains). 

The boundary attempts to lift north as a warm front Tuesday, but only 
makes it to around I-64. This means most of the area remains dry. 
Isolated showers and thunderstorms are possible in the afternoon 
along and south of a line from Staunton to Fredericksburg. The dry 
spell is going to be short lived as the warm front lifts north 
across the entire area on Wednesday, bringing the return of an 
active weather pattern that persists through the weekend.


KEY MESSAGE 2: Additional shower and thunderstorm chances
persist through this weekend.

Showers and thunderstorms will focus in the afternoon & evening 
hours each day. Increasing humidity will allow for PWATs ranging 
from the 75th-90th percentile, indicating potentially increased 
flooding concerns with any thunderstorms that do materialize. Severe 
thunderstorm probabilities continue to indicate the potential for 
severe thunderstorms during the Thursday-Sunday timeframe, with 
machine learning outputs remaining in the 15%-30% range. Still, that 
remains uncertain given the lack of defined synoptic support and 
abundant cloud cover over the region that limits instability.

As this synoptic pattern persists, temperatures gradually increase 
back to summertime normals, with elevated humidity contributing 
towards heat indices that will approach 100F across the metros late 
into the week. Looking ahead, deterministic models do show some 
signal for this front transitioning offshore towards the start of 
next week with drier air moving in from the west, potentially 
providing some relief from the humidity. For now, the primary 
weather feature remains as humid & rainy, along with increasing 
heat.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
A mix of MVFR to near-IFR CIGs continue to impact some 
terminals, but general improvements have been noted during the
past couple of hours.

VFR conditions return this afternoon as a front slowly moves south 
across the area. Another round of showers/thunderstorms are likely 
this afternoon, except at KMRB that will be north of the 
boundary. Dry and VFR conditions tonight through Wednesday 
morning. Daily shower and thunderstorm chances return Wednesday 
afternoon as that frontal boundary lifts back north across the 
area as a warm front.

Sub-VFR conditions will likely continue to be intermittent at 
terminals throughout the week as daily shower and thunderstorm 
chances persist, particularly in the afternoon & evening timeframes. 
South to southwesterly winds flow Wednesday through the end of the 
week.

&&

.MARINE...
Southerly channeling this morning is going to produce SCA 
conditions, especially the main channel of the southern 
Chesapeake Bay. A weak front slowly moves south across the 
waters today, though not before another round of showers and 
thunderstorms develop this afternoon. Special Marine Warnings 
are likely needed again today, especially south of the Bay 
Bridge and over the lower Tidal Potomac. Wind gusts in excess of
35 knots are the primary threat to mariners, in addition to 
lightning strikes. 

The front pushes south of the waters this evening. Dry conditions 
and sub-SCA winds expected Tuesday into Wednesday morning. The 
stalled boundary lifts back north over the area as a warm front by 
Wednesday afternoon. Southerly flow returns, and could approach SCA 
levels over the central Chesapeake Bay. Wednesday also brings with 
it the return of daily afternoon showers and thunderstorms. 

Southerly channeling over the waters are anticipated to produce SCA 
conditions Thursday afternoon through Friday. Showers & 
thunderstorms remain possible over the waters during this period 
(especially in the afternoon/evening hours) due to a stalled front 
nearby.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal levels remain elevated this morning, but minor tidal
flooding has begun to subside at Annapolis behind high tide.
Other sensitive locations likely top out at Action Stage. A 
brief period of lighter winds is expected Tuesday and that 
should prevent minor tidal flooding at all locations. Southerly 
flow returns Wednesday through the end of the week, bringing the
possibility of additional periods of coastal flooding.

&&
